source.title: Inscribed Objects from Harappa Excavations 1986–2007
source.publication: Corpus of Indus Seals and Inscriptions, Volume 3, Part 1, xliv–lviii
source.inspection: Extracted text checked against rendered source pages 5, 6 and 9; a publication-level observation, without direct object inspection
source.relation_to_prior_source: Same published introduction as the acquired 15-page witness; this 17-page public file includes preliminary book pages and has a different scan/hash.

assertions.assertion: The authors describe 22 copied steatite tablets from secondary Period 3B deposits outside Mound E's perimeter wall.
assertions.field_basis: source-reported material, group, context and dating

assertions.assertion: Six sealing fragments were lightly fired; a seventh jar-stopper was recovered unbaked.
assertions.field_basis: source-reported manufacture and recovery; precise closure contents unspecified

assertions.assertion: The authors identify stamped vessel sherds, impressed before firing and associated mainly with Period 3C pointed-base goblets.
assertions.field_basis: source-reported manufacture, vessel group and chronology

assertions.assertion: H1537's proposed date was revised to Period 3C after tool-mark comparison; H1539's marks were reconsidered as possibly animal-made.
assertions.field_basis: author re-examination; both absent from the audited observation export

assertions.assertion: Registration identifies the object; excavation-unit and item numbers preserve the context join.
assertions.field_basis: primary documentation of the identifier schema

assertions.assertion: Dates can follow find context or, for redeposited objects, assessments of material, style, technique and imagery.
assertions.field_basis: documented mixed basis of chronological labels

working_assumptions: CISI bases in the introduction and derivative export name the same intended published object; exact lot/item linkage still requires the basic-data catalogue.
Group descriptions are authored archaeological assertions, separate from our aggregate export computation.
Published secondary-deposit chronology describes recovery context and permits residual objects.
